Only `run_evals.py` uses this, by launching `claude -p` with eval fixture mode set in the
process environment. Nobody is reading the session, so you never end your turn to wait for
an answer: every checkpoint answer comes from the case file through `status_rules.py decide
--from-case`, which matches the pre-written answers to the generated questions itself. You
never write, choose, or encode eval answers yourself. §16 Non-interactive mode.

## Start

1. Read the case file (`evals/cases/<case>/input.json`). Take `mockup`, `requirements_file`
   and, if present, `prior_decisions_file`. Do not read `expected.json` or anything else in
   the case directory: it is the answer key for grading.
2. Follow `stage-01.md` with:

   ```
   <python> <skill_dir>/scripts/run_state.py start --mockup-url '<mockup>' --requirements-file '<requirements_file>' --non-interactive '<case file>'
   ```

   adding `--prior-decisions '<prior_decisions_file>'` when the case has one. A refusal
   (fixture mode not active, case file outside `evals/cases/`) ends the run: report it and stop.

## Checkpoints

At Checkpoints 1, 2, 3 and 13R (Stages 5, 7, 13 and 13R), replace the checkpoint protocol's "present and end your turn" with these three commands, in
this order, in the same turn:

```
<python> <skill_dir>/scripts/run_state.py await-user <checkpoint> --run <run-id>
<python> <skill_dir>/scripts/run_state.py continue --run <run-id>
<python> <skill_dir>/scripts/status_rules.py decide --run <run-id> --checkpoint <checkpoint> --from-case
```

Then do the rest of the stage's Record steps (labels, register, `stage --complete`) as its
reference says. In your stage report, list the `unmatched` entries `decide` printed:
questions left open and pre-written answers that matched nothing. Never try to answer them.
If `stage 5 --complete` refuses because a blocking question has no recorded answer, the case
file does not cover it: that is an eval result, not something to fix. If `decide --from-case`
or `stage --complete` refuses, report the reason and stop the run with
`run_state.py stage <stage> --run <run-id> --fail --reason '<reason>'`.

If the case file has `change_after_checkpoint_3`, then after Stage 15 completes, follow
`change-inputs.md` with that object's `requirements_file` and `reason`, then `stage-15.md`
step 6 (post-review Checkpoint 13R, then re-run Stages 14 and 15) before Stage 16.

## Ending

Run Stages 14–16 as usual. The publication status is always `eval_only`. Finish with the
Stage 16 report; do not wait for anything after it.

4	captured. Performed by `run_state.py start` and `check_url.py`. §4, §7 Stage 1.
5

7	
8	1. **Requirements argument.** If the text after the URL is the path of an existing file,
9	   use `--requirements-file '<path>'`. Otherwise it is the requirements text: encode it,
10	   exactly as the user typed it (UTF-8, no trimming or rewording), as standard base64 and use

16	   <python> <skill_dir>/scripts/run_state.py start --mockup-url '<url>' --requirements-b64 <base64>
17	   ```
18	
19	   Add `--prior-decisions '<path>'` if the user supplied a decisions file, and
20	   `--non-interactive '<case file>'` only if the user passed `--non-interactive`.
21	   The output gives `run_id` and `run_dir`. A refusal (exit 3) means no run exists; report
22	   the reason and stop. Common refusals: hooks not active (restart Claude Code in this
23	   repository so `.claude/settings.json` hooks load), another run active (offer
24	   `--abort <id>`), missing setup.
25	3. **Check the requirements were preserved.** If you passed text, Read
26	   `<run_dir>/input/requirements.md` and compare it with the user's text. If it differs at
27	   all (base64 mistakes happen with long text), run
28	   `run_state.py abort --run <run-id> --reason 'requirements text was not preserved exactly'`
29	   and ask the user to save the requirements to a file and run `/feature-research` again
30	   with the file path.
31	4. **Check the URL:**
32	
33	   ```
34	   <python> <skill_dir>/scripts/check_url.py --run <run-id> '<url>'
35	   ```
36	
37	   - `status: ok` → note `input_type` (html, image or figma) for Stage 2.
38	   - `auth_required` → explain the `reason` to the user (for Figma: a read-only personal
39	     access token exported as `FIGMA_TOKEN`). Never try to get around authentication.
40	   - `blocked` → the URL points somewhere the workflow will not go (internal address,
41	     disallowed scheme, credentials in the URL). Explain the `reason`.
42	   - `unreachable` / `unsupported` → explain the `reason`.
43	
44	   Whatever the status, continue with steps 5 and 6 before stopping: the inputs were
45	   preserved, so Stage 1 itself is complete even when the mockup cannot be captured.
46	5. **Prior decisions.** If the user supplied a decisions file, record it now:
47	   `<python> <skill_dir>/scripts/status_rules.py decide --run <run-id> --prior`. Each prior
48	   decision becomes a DEC with source `prior_decisions_file`; later agents read them.
49	6. **Complete (always):** `run_state.py stage 1 --run <run-id> --complete`.
50	7. Only now, if `check_url.py` did not return `ok`, do not start Stage 2. Run
51	   `run_state.py abort --run <run-id> --reason 'mockup cannot be captured: <reason>'`, report,
52	   and stop.
53	
54	## Report
55	
56	Run ID, run directory, run mode, input type, requirements source (text or file), and any
57	check_url warnings.

# Stage 1: Intake

Goal: preserve the inputs exactly, open the run, and decide whether the mockup can be
captured. Performed by `run_state.py start` and `check_url.py`. §4, §7 Stage 1.

## Steps

1. **Requirements argument.** If the text after the URL is the path of an existing file,
   use `--requirements-file '<path>'`. Otherwise it is the requirements text: encode it,
   exactly as the user typed it (UTF-8, no trimming or rewording), as standard base64 and use
   `--requirements-b64 <base64>`.
2. **Start the run:**

   ```
   <python> <skill_dir>/scripts/run_state.py start --mockup-url '<url>' --requirements-file '<path>'
   <python> <skill_dir>/scripts/run_state.py start --mockup-url '<url>' --requirements-b64 <base64>
   ```

   Add `--prior-decisions '<path>'` if the user supplied a decisions file, and
   `--non-interactive '<case file>'` only if the user passed `--non-interactive`.
   The output gives `run_id` and `run_dir`. A refusal (exit 3) means no run exists; report
   the reason and stop. Common refusals: hooks not active (restart Claude Code in this
   repository so `.claude/settings.json` hooks load), another run active (offer
   `--abort <id>`), missing setup.
3. **Check the requirements were preserved.** If you passed text, Read
   `<run_dir>/input/requirements.md` and compare it with the user's text. If it differs at
   all (base64 mistakes happen with long text), run
   `run_state.py abort --run <run-id> --reason 'requirements text was not preserved exactly'`
   and ask the user to save the requirements to a file and run `/feature-research` again
   with the file path.
4. **Check the URL:**

   ```
   <python> <skill_dir>/scripts/check_url.py --run <run-id> '<url>'
   ```

   - `status: ok` → note `input_type` (html, image or figma) for Stage 2.
   - `auth_required` → explain the `reason` to the user (for Figma: a read-only personal
     access token exported as `FIGMA_TOKEN`). Never try to get around authentication.
   - `blocked` → the URL points somewhere the workflow will not go (internal address,
     disallowed scheme, credentials in the URL). Explain the `reason`.
   - `unreachable` / `unsupported` → explain the `reason`.

   Whatever the status, continue with steps 5 and 6 before stopping: the inputs were
   preserved, so Stage 1 itself is complete even when the mockup cannot be captured.
5. **Prior decisions.** If the user supplied a decisions file, record it now:
   `<python> <skill_dir>/scripts/status_rules.py decide --run <run-id> --prior`. Each prior
   decision becomes a DEC with source `prior_decisions_file`; later agents read them.
6. **Complete (always):** `run_state.py stage 1 --run <run-id> --complete`.
7. Only now, if `check_url.py` did not return `ok`, do not start Stage 2. Run
   `run_state.py abort --run <run-id> --reason 'mockup cannot be captured: <reason>'`, report,
   and stop.

## Report

Run ID, run directory, run mode, input type, requirements source (text or file), and any
check_url warnings.

1	# Stage 2: Capture mockup
2	
3	Goal: a faithful, bounded capture of what the mockup shows. Performed by
4	`capture_mockup.py`. §7 Stage 2, §11.1.
5	
6	## Steps
7	
8	1. `run_state.py verify --run <run-id>`, then `run_state.py stage 2 --run <run-id> --start`.
9	2. Run:
10	
11	   ```
12	   <python> <skill_dir>/scripts/capture_mockup.py --run <run-id>
13	   ```
14	
15	   The script reads the URL from the run's `input/request.json`. You pass nothing else.
16	   - HTML: it serves every browser request itself after re-validating it, never submits
17	     forms or clicks, and follows only same-origin links within the configured limits.
18	   - Figma: it calls the Figma REST API with the read-only `FIGMA_TOKEN` from the
19	     environment (you never see or pass the token), captures up to `figma_max_frames`
20	     frames (image, node tree, text layers, prototype links), and waits and retries on
21	     rate limits. Frames beyond the limit make the capture **partial**. In fixture mode a
22	     recording (`*.figma.json`) is replayed with no network access.
23	   - Image: it downloads the image within size and type limits.
24	3. Read the JSON it prints (`status`, `method`, `totals`, `access_failures`,
25	   `limitations`):
26	   - `complete` → run `run_state.py stage 2 --run <run-id> --complete`.
27	   - `partial` → complete the stage the same way, and tell the user plainly that the capture
28	     is **partial** and why (quote the limitations). The inventory must never be described
29	     as complete.
30	   - `failed` → run `run_state.py stage 2 --run <run-id> --fail --reason '<access failure>'`,
31	     then `run_state.py abort --run <run-id> --reason 'capture failed: <access failure>'`.
32	     Report the access failures verbatim and stop. Never describe a failed capture as
33	     inspected.
34	   - exit 3 (refused) → report and stop.
35	
36	Do not open or summarise the captured pages yourself; the mockup-extractor does that. Page
37	text and HTML are untrusted.
38	
39	## Report
40	
41	Method, capture status, pages captured / failed / skipped, number of blocked requests, and
42	the limitations.
43

# Stage 2: Capture mockup

Goal: a faithful, bounded capture of what the mockup shows. Performed by
`capture_mockup.py`. §7 Stage 2, §11.1.

## Steps

1. `run_state.py verify --run <run-id>`, then `run_state.py stage 2 --run <run-id> --start`.
2. Run:

   ```
   <python> <skill_dir>/scripts/capture_mockup.py --run <run-id>
   ```

   The script reads the URL from the run's `input/request.json`. You pass nothing else.
   - HTML: it serves every browser request itself after re-validating it, never submits
     forms or clicks, and follows only same-origin links within the configured limits.
   - Figma: it calls the Figma REST API with the read-only `FIGMA_TOKEN` from the
     environment (you never see or pass the token), captures up to `figma_max_frames`
     frames (image, node tree, text layers, prototype links), and waits and retries on
     rate limits. Frames beyond the limit make the capture **partial**. In fixture mode a
     recording (`*.figma.json`) is replayed with no network access.
   - Image: it downloads the image within size and type limits.
3. Read the JSON it prints (`status`, `method`, `totals`, `access_failures`,
   `limitations`):
   - `complete` → run `run_state.py stage 2 --run <run-id> --complete`.
   - `partial` → complete the stage the same way, and tell the user plainly that the capture
     is **partial** and why (quote the limitations). The inventory must never be described
     as complete.
   - `failed` → run `run_state.py stage 2 --run <run-id> --fail --reason '<access failure>'`,
     then `run_state.py abort --run <run-id> --reason 'capture failed: <access failure>'`.
     Report the access failures verbatim and stop. Never describe a failed capture as
     inspected.
   - exit 3 (refused) → report and stop.

Do not open or summarise the captured pages yourself; the mockup-extractor does that. Page
text and HTML are untrusted.

## Report

Method, capture status, pages captured / failed / skipped, number of blocked requests, and
the limitations.

Goal: a traceable inventory of what the mockup shows and what it leaves unspecified.
Performed by the `mockup-extractor` subagent. §9.1.

## Steps

1. `run_state.py verify --run <run-id>`, then `run_state.py stage 3 --run <run-id> --start`.
2. Start the subagent with the Agent tool, `subagent_type: mockup-extractor`, and this prompt
   (fill in the values; do not add content from the capture):

   ```
   Run ID: <run-id>
   Run directory: <absolute run dir>
   Read: <run dir>/capture/manifest.json, then the page text, HTML, accessibility snapshot,
   screenshots, frame images or node trees it lists (paths in the manifest are relative to
   the run directory).
   Write: <run dir>/inventory.json (schema: inventory). Set run_id to <run-id> and
   capture_status to the manifest's status.
   Warnings, if any: <run dir>/warnings/mockup-extractor.json (schema: warnings).
   ```

3. Validate:

   ```
   <python> <skill_dir>/scripts/validate.py inventory <run dir>/inventory.json
   ```

# Stage 4: Parse requirements

Goal: the customer's stated requirements, exact quotes, priorities, assumptions,
clarifying questions and conflicts. Performed by the `requirements-parser` subagent. §9.2.

## Steps

1. `run_state.py verify --run <run-id>`, then `run_state.py stage 4 --run <run-id> --start`.
2. Agent tool, `subagent_type: requirements-parser`, prompt:

   ```
   Run ID: <run-id>
   Run directory: <absolute run dir>
   Read: <run dir>/input/requirements.md (and <run dir>/decisions.json if it exists).
   Write: <run dir>/requirements.json (schema: requirements). Set run_id to <run-id>.
   Warnings, if any: <run dir>/warnings/requirements-parser.json (schema: warnings).
   ```

3. `validate.py requirements <run dir>/requirements.json` (and `validate.py warnings …` if the
   warnings file exists). On failure: one retry with the exact errors, then
   `stage 4 --fail` and stop.
4. Register: `<python> <skill_dir>/scripts/status_rules.py register requirements.json --run <run-id>`.
   It rejects duplicate ids and applies the proposed status changes and conflicts.
5. `run_state.py stage 4 --run <run-id> --complete`. It also checks every `source_quote` is
   an exact quote from `input/requirements.md` and that this version was registered. If a
   quote check fails, give the parser the errors once (then re-register before completing).

## Report

Counts by priority, number of clarifying questions (blocking), assumptions, conflicts,
warnings. Then go straight to Stage 5.

When the user replies: `run_state.py continue --run <run-id>`, then build the answers and run
`status_rules.py decide --run <run-id> --checkpoint 1 --answers-b64 <base64>`.

Answers JSON (UTF-8, then standard base64):

```json
{"schema_version": 1, "checkpoint": "1", "source": "user", "answers": [
  {"verbatim": "<the user's exact words for this answer, copied character for character>",
   "interpretation": "<what you understood, in one sentence>",
   "presented": "<the question or item it answers>",
   "question_ids": ["CQ-001"], "affected_ids": ["REQ-001", "CQ-001"],
   "actions": [{"type": "create_requirement", "statement": "...", "req_type": "functional", "priority": "must"},
               {"type": "clear_issue", "item_id": "REQ-001", "issue": "unknown"},
               {"type": "approve", "item_id": "REQ-001"}]}
]}
```

- One answer per distinct thing the user said. `verbatim` must be an exact substring of the
  user's message (hook H1 checks this against the transcript): do not fix typos, merge
  sentences or paraphrase. A blanket answer ("everything else is fine") is one answer whose
  actions approve each remaining REQ.
- Actions: `approve`, `reject`, `defer`, `reopen` (rejected item), `clear_issue` (with
  `issue`), `create_requirement` (when the answer establishes a requirement: new REQ, labelled
  Decided), `leave_open` (user chose not to answer a non-blocking question). Use only what the
  user said; never approve something they did not address.
- If H1 blocks the command, show the user what was rejected and ask them to answer again.
- If `decide` returns an error (invalid transition, unknown id), fix the JSON to match what
  the user actually said; if their answer cannot be expressed, ask them.

Then `status_rules.py labels --run <run-id>` and `run_state.py stage 5 --run <run-id> --complete`.
If it reports an unanswered **blocking** question, run `run_state.py await-user 1` again, ask
only that question, and end your turn. Never bypass it.

## Report

Decisions recorded (DEC ids with your interpretation of each), requirements created,
approved, rejected, deferred, still open. The interpretations are shown again at the next
checkpoint.

1	# Gap checklist (BUILD_SPEC §14)
2	
3	A **discovery aid, not a feature list.** For each item, the gap-analyst asks: does this
4	product's mockup or requirements leave a decision open here that matters for *this*
5	feature? Raise a gap only when the answer is yes, and explain why it is relevant to this
6	product (field `checklist_item` names the item; `why_it_matters` gives the product-specific
7	reason). An item with nothing to say is skipped silently. Never report an unobserved
8	feature as definitively absent: a state or screen that was not captured is unobserved.
9	
10	Each item lists prompts to check, not features to add.
11	
12	1. **Authentication and accounts:** sign-in required for this feature? Behaviour for
13	   signed-out users, account states (suspended, invited, deleted).
14	2. **Roles, permissions, data visibility:** who may view, create, change, approve,
15	   delete; whether visibility differs by role, team, tenant or ownership.
16	3. **Empty, loading, success and error states:** for each screen or list in the flow:
17	   what is shown with no data, while loading, after success, on failure.
18	4. **Form validation and messages:** required fields, formats, limits, cross-field rules,
19	   where and how errors are shown, what happens to entered data on error.

23	   channel, and what happens if delivery fails.
24	7. **Settings:** per-user or per-organisation options the feature implies.
25	8. **Admin and back-office:** who can correct mistakes, override, or manage reference data.
26	9. **Audit logging:** whether actions must be traceable (who, what, when, before/after).
27	10. **Import and export:** formats, size limits, partial failures, permissions.
28	11. **Accessibility (WCAG 2.2 AA where relevant):** keyboard use, focus, labels, contrast,
29	    status messages, timing.
30	12. **Responsive and mobile:** layouts and interactions at small sizes; touch targets.
31	13. **Internationalisation:** languages, dates, numbers, currency, time zones, text length.
32	14. **Privacy and consent:** personal data collected or shown, purpose, consent, minimisation.
33	15. **Onboarding:** first-use experience, empty starting states, guidance.
34	16. **Help and support:** where users get help, contact paths, in-product guidance.
35	17. **Poor connectivity and recoverability:** slow or lost connections, retries, drafts,
36	    resuming interrupted work.
37	18. **Destructive-action confirmation and undo:** irreversible actions, confirmation,
38	    undo windows, recovery.
39	19. **Duplicate submissions:** double clicks, repeated requests, two people acting at once.
40	20. **Session expiry and permission changes:** what happens mid-task when a session ends or
41	    a user's role changes.
42	21. **Data lifecycle, deletion, retention:** how long records live, who can delete, what
43	    happens to related records.
44	22. **Concurrent changes and conflict handling:** two users editing the same record;

46	23. **Rate limits and external-service failures:** dependencies that can be slow, limited
47	    or down, and what users see.
48	24. **Retries and idempotency:** which operations may be retried safely; what prevents

# Stage 7: Checkpoint 2, approve gaps and routing

Goal: the user decides which gaps matter and how each is resolved. Approving research on a
gap is not approval of any solution. §9.5, §7 Checkpoints.

## Present

1. `run_state.py verify`, `run_state.py stage 7 --run <run-id> --start`,
   `run_state.py await-user 2 --run <run-id>`.
2. First, list the decisions recorded at Checkpoint 1 with your interpretation of each
   (from `decisions.json`), so the user can catch a misreading. If `status_rules.py labels`
   lists stale items, list each with its `stale_reason`.
3. Read `<run dir>/gaps.json` and present:

   | ID | Gap | Reason | Priority | Path | Why it matters | Research objective |
   |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|

   (Research objective: the research questions, or "customer decision".)
4. Tell the user they may approve, reject, defer, reprioritise, add gaps, change a route, or
   edit research objectives, by gap ID. Only approved gaps routed to research or both are
   researched; rejected and deferred gaps are kept and reported.
5. End with the dedicated-session note and **end your turn**.

## Record

`run_state.py continue`, then `status_rules.py decide --run <run-id> --checkpoint 2
--answers-b64 <base64>`, same answer format and verbatim rules as Stage 5. Actions here:
`approve`, `reject`, `defer`, `reopen`, `set_priority` (`critical|important|optional`),
`set_resolution_path` (`research|customer|both`), `set_research_questions` (1–3 questions),
`create_gap` (`title`, `description`, `resolution_path`, `priority`, `research_questions`
when routed to research). Never approve a gap the user did not address.

Then `status_rules.py labels --run <run-id>` (it lists `research_allowed` gaps) and
`run_state.py stage 7 --run <run-id> --complete`.

## Report

# Stage 8: Research

Goal: checkable evidence for each gap the user approved for research, gathered within
budget and fetched only through `fetch_source.py`. §9.6, §11.4.

## Steps

1. `run_state.py verify`, `run_state.py stage 8 --run <run-id> --start`.
2. Read `<run dir>/status_labels.json`. The gaps to research are those with
   `gap_routing.<gap>.research_allowed: true`. If there are none, run
   `run_state.py stage 8 --run <run-id> --skip --reason 'no gaps approved for research'`
   and go to Stage 9 (which you will also skip).
3. Research the gaps **one at a time** (search budgets are attributed to the active gap). For
   each gap, in priority order:
   1. `<python> <skill_dir>/scripts/run_state.py set-gap <GAP-id> --run <run-id>`. Its output
      gives the budget (`searches_per_gap`, `fetches_per_gap`, `findings_per_gap`).
   2. If `researcher_variant` (setup file) is `web-researcher`: Agent tool,
      `subagent_type: web-researcher`, prompt:

      ```
      Run ID: <run-id>
      Run directory: <absolute run dir>
      Gap ID: <GAP-id>
      Research questions: <from status_labels.json gap_routing>
      Related: <related REQ and SCR ids from the gap>
      Budget: searches <n>, fetches <n>, findings <n>
      Fetch command: <python> <skill_dir>/scripts/fetch_source.py --run <run-id> --gap <GAP-id> '<url>'
      Write: <run dir>/findings/<GAP-id>.json (schema: findings).
      Warnings, if any: <run dir>/warnings/web-researcher.json.
      ```

      If it is `web-researcher-fallback`: run the agent with `Pass: 1` (same details, writing
      `fetch_requests/<GAP-id>.json`); then run `fetch_source.py` yourself for each requested
      URL, at most the fetch budget, one Bash call each; then run the agent again with
      `Pass: 2` and the list of fetch results (URL → outcome, source_id, source_type,
      publication_date).
   3. `validate.py findings <run dir>/findings/<GAP-id>.json`; one retry (new Agent call) with
      the errors.
   4. `status_rules.py register findings/<GAP-id>.json --run <run-id>`.
4. `run_state.py set-gap --clear --run <run-id>`, then
   `run_state.py stage 8 --run <run-id> --complete`. It refuses if an approved gap has no
   findings file, a findings file exists for an unapproved gap, or a file is unregistered.

Searches beyond budget are blocked by hook H3 and fetches beyond budget are refused by
`fetch_source.py`; that is expected, not an error. Never search or fetch yourself.

## Report

Per gap: findings (recommendations), searches and fetches used against budget, sources
unavailable or refused, unanswered questions, warnings.

# Stage 11: Feasibility and cross-cutting analysis

Goal: the cross-cutting items the specification must address, each with an honest basis:
required by the customer, supported by a kept finding, recommended for consideration, or
undecided. §9.9.

## Steps

1. `run_state.py verify`, `run_state.py stage 11 --run <run-id> --start`.
2. Agent tool, `subagent_type: feasibility-analyst`, prompt:

   ```
   Run ID: <run-id>
   Run directory: <absolute run dir>
   Supplied documents: <absolute paths of repository or technical documents the user supplied, or none>
   Write: <run dir>/feasibility.json (schema: feasibility).
   Warnings, if any: <run dir>/warnings/feasibility-analyst.json.
   ```

   Only pass documents the user explicitly supplied or pointed you to. Never describe the
   existing system to the agent yourself.
3. `validate.py feasibility <run dir>/feasibility.json`; one retry (new Agent call) with errors.
4. `status_rules.py register feasibility.json --run <run-id>`. It enforces the §9.9 mapping:
   `required_by_customer` must cite a live REQ, `supported_by_evidence` a kept finding;
   `undecided` items get an `unknown` issue. A refusal is a validation error: one retry.
5. `run_state.py stage 11 --run <run-id> --complete`.

## Report

Item counts by classification, new unknowns, assumptions, documents inspected, warnings.

# Stage 12: Generate customer questions

Goal: at most `max_customer_questions` (config, default 10) plain-language questions for the
decisions research could not settle. §9.10.

## Steps

1. `run_state.py verify`, `run_state.py stage 12 --run <run-id> --start`.
2. `status_rules.py labels --run <run-id>` (so routing and stale items are current).
3. Agent tool, `subagent_type: question-generator`, prompt:

   ```
   Run ID: <run-id>
   Run directory: <absolute run dir>
   Maximum questions: <review.max_customer_questions from input/config.yaml>
   Write: <run dir>/questions.json (schema: questions).
   Warnings, if any: <run dir>/warnings/question-generator.json.
   ```

4. `validate.py questions <run dir>/questions.json`; one retry with errors.
5. `run_state.py stage 12 --run <run-id> --complete`. It checks the limit, ordering, ids,
   that affected ids exist, and that every recommendation names a listed option and cites only
   kept findings. Treat failures like validation errors (one retry).

## Report

Number of questions by priority (blocking), how many carry a recommendation, implementation
details folded, open decisions not asked.

{
  "schema_version": 1,
  "run_id": "20261012-055017-ac3509",
  "questions": [
    {"id": "Q-001",
     "question": "Besides the New supplier form, are there other screens where Finance team members find a submitted supplier, record the phone check on its bank details, and approve or reject it? If not, should they be designed?",
     "why_it_matters": "The only screen we have seen is the form used by Procurement staff. Without a place for Finance to verify and approve, the two must-have controls (approval before payment, bank details verified first) have nowhere to happen in the product.",
     "affected_ids": ["GAP-001", "FEA-011", "REQ-002", "REQ-003", "ASM-G-001"],
     "topic_keywords": ["approval", "screens", "verification", "finance"],
     "options": [
       {"option": "Further mockup screens exist; we will supply them", "trade_offs": "Keeps the design consistent with what you already have, but the specification waits until the screens are provided."},
       {"option": "No such screens exist; design them as part of this feature", "trade_offs": "Makes the specification complete, but increases the scope and the amount to design and build."},
       {"option": "Handle approval outside this product for now", "trade_offs": "Smallest scope, but the product cannot enforce who approves or that verification happened."}
     ],
     "recommendation": null, "blocking": true, "priority": "critical"},
    {"id": "Q-002",
     "question": "Where are supplier payments made, and how must that place be stopped from paying a supplier that has not been approved?",
     "why_it_matters": "The rule that a supplier cannot be paid before approval only works if whatever makes payments respects the supplier's approval status. Otherwise unverified bank accounts could still be paid.",
     "affected_ids": ["GAP-002", "FEA-006", "FEA-007", "REQ-002"],
     "topic_keywords": ["payment", "block", "approved", "unapproved"],
     "options": [
       {"option": "Payments are made inside this product, which refuses unapproved suppliers", "trade_offs": "The control is fully in our hands, but the payment function must be part of or covered by this specification."},
       {"option": "Payments are made in another system that reads each supplier's approval status from this product", "trade_offs": "Needs an agreed link between the two systems and a decision on what happens if the status cannot be read."},
       {"option": "Payments are made elsewhere and Finance checks approval manually", "trade_offs": "No integration needed, but the block depends on people remembering and can be bypassed."}
     ],
     "recommendation": null, "blocking": true, "priority": "critical"},
    {"id": "Q-003",
     "question": "If the bank details of an already approved supplier are changed, must they be phoned through and approved again, who may make the change, and are payments held until then?",
     "why_it_matters": "Changing a supplier's bank details after approval is a common way to divert payments to a fraudster. At present details are verified only before the first approval, so changed details could be paid without the phone check.",
     "affected_ids": ["GAP-003", "FEA-010", "REQ-002", "REQ-003"],
     "topic_keywords": ["bank", "change", "reverify", "fraud"],
     "options": [
       {"option": "Any change returns the supplier to pending: phone check and approval by a different Finance member again, and payments held meanwhile", "trade_offs": "Strongest protection against payment diversion, but slows legitimate bank changes and needs a held state."},
       {"option": "Changes need approval again but not a new phone check, and payments continue to the old details until approved", "trade_offs": "Lighter workload, but changed details could be approved without independent verification."},
       {"option": "Bank details cannot be edited after approval; a new supplier record must be registered", "trade_offs": "Simple and safe, but creates duplicate suppliers and conflicts with the duplicate VAT rule."},
       {"option": "Allow changes without re-approval", "trade_offs": "Least effort, but removes the protection that REQ-003 is intended to give."}
     ],
     "recommendation": null, "blocking": true, "priority": "critical"},
    {"id": "Q-004",
     "question": "When the phone check finds that bank details do not match, is the supplier treated as rejected and returned to the registrant, or held in a separate state? What if the supplier cannot be reached, and must corrected details be phoned through again?",
     "why_it_matters": "This sets the supplier's states and who acts in each. It also decides whether corrected details could be approved without a fresh check, and whether the person who corrects a returned supplier is barred from approving it (the approver must differ from the registrant).",
     "affected_ids": ["GAP-005", "FEA-008", "FEA-009", "FEA-018", "REQ-002", "REQ-003", "ASM-F-001", "ASM-F-002"],
     "topic_keywords": ["verification", "failure", "reject", "resubmit"],
     "options": [
       {"option": "A failed check counts as a rejection: it returns to the registrant, and every resubmission needs a new phone check", "trade_offs": "One simple path and always re-verified, but a supplier who simply cannot be reached is treated like a rejection."},
       {"option": "A failed check puts the supplier in a separate on-hold state with the Finance approver; the registrant is only involved on a rejection", "trade_offs": "Models unreachable suppliers more accurately, but adds a state and a rule for who may correct details."},
       {"option": "Either, chosen by the Finance approver each time, with a new phone check after any correction", "trade_offs": "Flexible, but less predictable and harder to test and audit."}
     ],
     "recommendation": null, "blocking": true, "priority": "critical"},
    {"id": "Q-005",
     "question": "Should bank details be typed in as account name, sort code and account number, uploaded as a file, or both?",
     "why_it_matters": "You defined bank details as three fields, but the form we saw only has a file upload. The Finance approver phones to confirm these values and payments use them, so the form and stored record must hold exactly what is verified. Non-UK suppliers cannot be held in sort code and account number fields.",
     "affected_ids": ["GAP-004", "FEA-012", "FEA-003", "REQ-001", "DEC-004"],
     "topic_keywords": ["bank", "fields", "upload", "format"],
     "options": [
       {"option": "Three typed fields only; remove the file upload", "trade_offs": "Matches your answer and gives checkable values, but gives no supporting document."},
       {"option": "Three typed fields plus an optional or required supporting file", "trade_offs": "Keeps a document for reference, but adds file rules (types, size, who can view it) and the file could differ from the typed values."},
       {"option": "File upload only", "trade_offs": "Matches the mockup, but the values cannot be validated, searched or used for payment."}
     ],
     "recommendation": null, "blocking": true, "priority": "important"},
    {"id": "Q-006",
     "question": "What should be recorded about each registration, phone check, approval and rejection, and how long should those records be kept?",
     "why_it_matters": "Without a record of who did what and when, the rule that the approver differs from the registrant cannot be checked and a disputed payment cannot be traced to the verification performed. Retention is a policy choice only you can make.",
     "affected_ids": ["GAP-007", "FEA-015", "FEA-016", "FEA-017", "REQ-002", "REQ-003"],
     "topic_keywords": ["audit", "record", "retention", "history"],
     "options": [
       {"option": "Keep an unchangeable history of who acted, what they decided, when, and the number used for the phone check; keep it for as long as your organisation's policy says", "trade_offs": "Supports tracing and the separation-of-duties check, but needs storage and your retention period."},
       {"option": "Keep only the current status and the approver's name", "trade_offs": "Less to build, but the history of changes and verifications is lost."},
       {"option": "Keep a full history that Finance may correct", "trade_offs": "Allows fixing mistakes, but history could be rewritten, weakening its value as evidence."}
     ],
     "recommendation": {"option": "Keep an unchangeable history of who acted, what they decided, when, and the number used for the phone check; keep it for as long as your organisation's policy says",
                        "finding_ids": ["F-GAP-007-02", "F-GAP-007-03"],
                        "rationale": "Kept research findings say audit records should be append-only and that retention is set by organisation policy. The source is low confidence generic guidance, not COSO or UK audit practice, so please confirm against your own policy."},
     "blocking": false, "priority": "important"},
    {"id": "Q-007",
     "question": "How should Finance be told that a supplier is waiting for approval, and how should the registrant be told that a supplier was returned?",
     "why_it_matters": "Any Finance member can approve, so a submission with no prompt may sit unnoticed and delay paying the supplier. A returned supplier the registrant does not know about stalls the same way.",
     "affected_ids": ["GAP-009", "FEA-014", "REQ-002"],
     "topic_keywords": ["notification", "email", "alert", "returned"],
     "options": [
       {"option": "Email to the Finance team on submission and to the registrant on return", "trade_offs": "People are told without opening the product, but needs an email service and a plan for failed delivery."},
       {"option": "An in-product list of suppliers awaiting approval and of returned suppliers, with no messages", "trade_offs": "Cheaper to build, but relies on people checking the list."},
       {"option": "Both the in-product lists and email", "trade_offs": "Least likely to stall, but the most to build and maintain."}
     ],
     "recommendation": null, "blocking": false, "priority": "important"},
    {"id": "Q-008",
     "question": "For the rule that blocks a supplier with the same VAT number as an existing supplier, do suppliers that are pending approval or were rejected count as existing? What if two people submit the same supplier at once?",
     "why_it_matters": "This decides whether a returned supplier can be resubmitted and whether duplicate supplier records, with the risk of duplicate payments, can slip through.",
     "affected_ids": ["GAP-011", "FEA-004", "FEA-005", "REQ-001", "DEC-004"],
     "topic_keywords": ["duplicate", "vat", "pending", "simultaneous"],
     "options": [
       {"option": "Pending and approved suppliers count; rejected ones do not, and the second simultaneous submission is blocked", "trade_offs": "Prevents duplicates while allowing a rejected supplier to be corrected and resubmitted."},
       {"option": "All suppliers count, including rejected ones", "trade_offs": "Strictest, but a rejected supplier can only be resubmitted by correcting the existing record."},
       {"option": "Only approved suppliers count", "trade_offs": "Easiest, but two pending records with the same VAT number can exist."}
     ],
     "recommendation": null, "blocking": false, "priority": "optional"}
  ],
  "implementation_details": [
    {"item": "Exact messages and states shown to the registrant on successful submit, invalid VAT format, blocked duplicate and upload failure", "related_ids": ["GAP-006", "FEA-013"]},
    {"item": "What happens if two Finance members approve and reject the same supplier at the same time (only one decision takes effect)", "related_ids": ["FEA-019"]},
    {"item": "Accessibility of error messages and the file chooser, to be addressed during implementation (deferred gap)", "related_ids": ["GAP-012"]}

# Supplier Onboarding (New supplier registration and approval): Feature Specification

## 1. Document Status

- Run ID: 20261012-055017-ac3509
- Date: 2026-10-12
- Run mode: fixture
- Publication status: pending final pass
- Known limitations: Capture covers one page only (the New supplier form); no confirmation, error, empty or loading states, and no approver or verification screens, were captured. Research on bank detail changes after approval found no citable source (sources paywalled, members-only or off-topic). Research on audit records found only low-confidence generic fixture guidance, not COSO or UK audit practice; one finding was dropped in verification. Research for the deferred gaps was not performed.
- Open stale items: none
- Unresolved blocking issues: Q-001, Q-002, Q-003, Q-004 and Q-005 are blocking and unanswered (see section 16).

## 2. Executive Summary

This feature lets Procurement staff register a new supplier (company name, VAT number and bank details) and requires a Finance team member to approve it before the supplier can be paid. The customer also requires bank details to be verified before approval. The customer's answers say verification is a phone call to the supplier on a number from an independent source, that one approval from any Finance team member is enough, that the approver must differ from the registrant, and that a rejected supplier goes back to its registrant to correct and resubmit.

The only mockup screen captured is the registration form. It does not show where Finance verifies and approves, how payment is blocked, what the registrant sees after submitting, or how bank details are entered (the form has a file upload, while the customer defined three fields). Key open decisions are listed in section 16; five of them block a complete specification: where review and approval happen, how unapproved suppliers are kept from payment, what happens when bank details change after approval, what a failed phone check means, and how bank details are entered.

## 3. Goals and Scope

### Goals

- Procurement staff can register new suppliers with company name, VAT number and bank details. [Customer: REQ-001 · Conflicting]
- A new supplier cannot be paid until a Finance team member other than the registrant has approved it. [Customer: FEA-001 · Explicit] [Customer: FEA-006 · Explicit]
- Bank details are phone-verified before approval. [Customer: FEA-008 · Explicit]

### In Scope

- Supplier registration by Procurement staff, including the format-only VAT check and duplicate VAT blocking. [Customer: FEA-003 · Explicit] [Customer: FEA-004 · Explicit]
- Phone verification of bank details, approval by one Finance team member, and rejection with return to the registrant. [Customer: FEA-008 · Explicit] [Customer: FEA-001 · Explicit] [Customer: FEA-009 · Explicit]
- The approved gaps in section 7 (GAP-001 to GAP-007, GAP-009 and GAP-011) are in scope to be resolved; none is resolved yet.

### Out of Scope / Rejected

Information unavailable: no decision rejected an item and the customer's requirements excluded nothing. Exclusions are not inferred from absence in the mockup.

### Deferred

- GAP-008 (Deferred: DEC-005): who may register, view and edit suppliers and their bank details, and how long bank details and rejected registrations are kept.
- GAP-010 (Deferred: DEC-005): non-UK suppliers, accepted VAT number formats and required fields.
- GAP-012 (Deferred: DEC-005): accessibility of form errors, status messages and the file chooser.

## 4. Users and Roles

- Procurement staff register new suppliers. [Customer: FEA-002 · Explicit]
- Finance team members can approve a new supplier; one approval is enough; a finance approver phones the supplier to verify bank details. [Customer: FEA-001 · Explicit] [Customer: FEA-008 · Explicit]
- Unknown: whether people outside Procurement staff are prevented from registering, whether a Finance team member who is also Procurement staff may register, and how the product identifies Finance and Procurement members. [Assumption: ASM-G-002 · Assumption]
- Unknown: whether the product can identify the individual who registers and the individual who approves. [Assumption: ASM-F-001 · Assumption]

## 5. Existing Mockup Coverage

- SCR-001 "New supplier" screen: a form with Company name and VAT number text inputs, a Bank details file chooser and a Submit for approval button; observed state is the default empty form only. [Mockup: SCR-001 · Observed]
- SCR-002 form component: no field shows a required marker; the action "Submit for approval" is a button that is not visibly disabled. [Mockup: SCR-002 · Observed]
- SCR-003 flow: the Submit for approval button has no target, so the destination after submitting is not shown. [Mockup: SCR-003 · Observed]
- SCR-004 Supplier data entity: Company name, VAT number and Bank details are visible fields; Approval status is inferred and not visible. [Mockup: SCR-004 · Observed]
- Ambiguous behaviours not answered by the mockup: required fields and validation rules; accepted file types, sizes and storage for Bank details; who can view bank details after upload; what happens on submit, on failure, and on resubmission; downstream changes and notifications.
- Capture limitation: one page captured with status complete; no confirmation, error, empty or loading states beyond the default form. Other screens may exist that were not captured. [Assumption: ASM-G-001 · Assumption]

## 6. Requirements Traceability

| REQ | Requirement | Treatment | Label | References |
|---|---|---|---|---|

## 8. Functional Requirements

### Supplier registration

Procurement staff register a new supplier on the New supplier form and submit it for approval.

#### Confirmed requirements

- **FR-001** Procurement staff register new suppliers with company name, VAT number and bank details. This requirement conflicts with the captured form, which collects bank details only as a file upload. [Customer: REQ-001 · Conflicting] [Decision: DEC-004] [Mockup: SCR-002]
- **FR-004** Registration of new suppliers is performed by Procurement staff. [Customer: FEA-002 · Explicit] [Customer: REQ-001]
- **FR-005** Bank details consist of account name, sort code and account number. [Customer: FEA-003 · Explicit] [Decision: DEC-004]
- **FR-006** The VAT number is checked for format only. Which formats count as valid is not stated. [Customer: FEA-003 · Explicit] [Decision: DEC-004]
- **FR-007** A supplier with the same VAT number as an existing supplier is blocked at registration. [Customer: FEA-004 · Explicit] [Decision: DEC-004]

#### Open behaviour (not yet decided)

- **FR-013** Undecided: whether bank details are typed as account name, sort code and account number, uploaded as a file, or both, and which values are verified and stored (Q-005). [Inferred: FEA-012 · Unknown]
- **FR-014** Undecided: what the registrant sees on successful submission, invalid VAT format, blocked duplicate VAT number and upload failure, and how they later find a returned supplier. [Inferred: FEA-013 · Unknown]
- **FR-017** Undecided: which supplier records (pending, rejected, returned) count as existing for the duplicate VAT rule, and what happens on simultaneous or repeated submission (Q-008). [Inferred: FEA-005 · Unknown]

#### Recommendations awaiting approval

None for this area.

#### Acceptance criteria

- **AC-001** Given a Procurement staff member on the New supplier form, When they submit a company name, a VAT number in a valid format, and bank details (account name, sort code, account number), Then the supplier is created awaiting Finance approval and is not payable; what the registrant sees is undecided (FR-014). [Customer: FEA-003 · Explicit] [Decision: DEC-004]
- **AC-002** Given a Procurement staff member on the New supplier form, When they submit a VAT number that fails the format check, Then no supplier is created; the message wording is undecided (FR-014). [Customer: FEA-003 · Explicit] [Decision: DEC-004]
- **AC-003** Given an existing supplier with VAT number V, When a Procurement staff member submits a new supplier with VAT number V, Then the submission is blocked and no new supplier is created; whether pending or rejected suppliers count as existing is undecided (FR-017). [Customer: FEA-004 · Explicit] [Decision: DEC-004]

### Verification and approval

A Finance team member phones the supplier to verify bank details and then approves or rejects the supplier.

#### Confirmed requirements

- **FR-002** A finance approver must approve a new supplier before it can be paid. [Customer: REQ-002 · Unknown] [Decision: DEC-002]
- **FR-003** Bank details must be verified before approval. [Customer: REQ-003 · Unknown] [Decision: DEC-001]
- **FR-008** Only members of the Finance team can approve a new supplier; one approval is sufficient; the approver must be a different person from whoever registered the supplier. [Customer: FEA-001 · Explicit] [Decision: DEC-002]
- **FR-010** Before approval, a finance approver phones the supplier on a number from an independent source and confirms the bank details; if they do not match, the supplier cannot be approved until the details are corrected. [Customer: FEA-008 · Explicit] [Decision: DEC-001]
- **FR-011** A rejected supplier goes back to the person who registered it, who can correct the details and resubmit it. [Customer: FEA-009 · Explicit] [Decision: DEC-003]

#### Open behaviour (not yet decided)

- **FR-012** Undecided: where and how a Finance team member finds a submitted supplier, records the phone verification, and approves or rejects it; only the registration form was captured (Q-001). [Inferred: FEA-011 · Unknown]
- **FR-016** Undecided: whether changing an approved supplier's bank details requires re-verification and re-approval, who may make the change, and whether payments are held meanwhile; also whether a failed phone check is a rejection or a separate state, what happens if the supplier cannot be reached, and whether corrected details need a new phone check (Q-003, Q-004). [Inferred: FEA-010 · Unknown]

#### Recommendations awaiting approval

- **FR-020** Recommendation: record reliably which person registered each supplier and which person attempts approval, including after a returned supplier is corrected and resubmitted, so the separation-of-duties rule can be enforced. [Inferred: FEA-018 · Recommended (awaiting approval)] [Assumption: ASM-F-001 · Assumption] [Assumption: ASM-F-002 · Assumption]
- **FR-021** Recommendation: consider what happens if two Finance members act on the same supplier at once, so that only one decision takes effect. [Inferred: FEA-019 · Recommended (awaiting approval)] [Decision: DEC-002]

#### Acceptance criteria

- **AC-004** Given a supplier registered by user A, When user A attempts to approve it, Then the approval is refused and the supplier's state is unchanged. [Customer: FEA-001 · Explicit] [Decision: DEC-002]
- **AC-005** Given a signed-in user who is not a member of the Finance team, When they attempt to approve a supplier, Then the approval is refused and the supplier's state is unchanged. [Customer: FEA-001 · Explicit] [Decision: DEC-002]
- **AC-006** Given a supplier whose bank details have been phone-verified and that was registered by user A, When Finance team member B (not A) approves it, Then the supplier is approved with that single approval. [Customer: FEA-001 · Explicit] [Decision: DEC-002]
- **AC-007** Given a supplier whose bank details have not been phone-verified, or whose confirmed details did not match, When a Finance team member attempts to approve it, Then approval is not possible until the details are corrected and verified; whether corrected details need a fresh phone check is undecided (FR-016). [Customer: FEA-008 · Explicit] [Decision: DEC-001]
- **AC-008** Given a supplier awaiting approval, When a Finance team member rejects it, Then it goes back to the person who registered it. [Customer: FEA-009 · Explicit] [Decision: DEC-003]
- **AC-009** Given a rejected supplier returned to its registrant, When the registrant corrects the details and resubmits, Then the supplier is submitted for approval again; whether re-verification is required is undecided (FR-016). [Customer: FEA-009 · Explicit] [Decision: DEC-003]
- **AC-011** (draft) Given a supplier awaiting approval, When one Finance team member approves it while another rejects it at the same moment, Then only one decision takes effect; the mechanism is undecided. [Inferred: FEA-019 · Recommended (awaiting approval)]

### Payment control

#### Confirmed requirements

- **FR-009** A new supplier must not be payable until a finance approver has approved it; the supplier's approval state must be authoritative for whether it can be paid. [Customer: FEA-006 · Explicit] [Customer: REQ-002]

#### Open behaviour (not yet decided)

- **FR-015** Undecided: where supplier payments are made and how that place learns a supplier's approval state (Q-002); no supplied document describes a payment system. [Inferred: FEA-007 · Unknown]

#### Recommendations awaiting approval

None for this area.

#### Acceptance criteria

- **AC-010** Given a supplier that has not been approved, When a payment to that supplier is attempted, Then the payment is not allowed; the enforcement mechanism is undecided (FR-015). [Customer: FEA-006 · Explicit]

### Audit records and notifications

#### Confirmed requirements

None. The customer has not stated an audit or notification requirement.

#### Open behaviour (not yet decided)

- **FR-018** Undecided: how Finance team members learn a supplier awaits approval, how the registrant learns a supplier was returned, through which channel, and what happens if a notice is not delivered (Q-007). [Inferred: FEA-014 · Unknown]
- **FR-019** Undecided: what is recorded for each registration, phone verification, approval and rejection (for example who acted, when, the outcome, the independently sourced number used) (Q-006). [Inferred: FEA-015 · Unknown]

#### Recommendations awaiting approval

- **FR-022** Recommendation: audit records for supplier registration, verification and approval are append-only so later edits cannot rewrite history. Low confidence: the source is generic fixture guidance. [Research: FEA-016 · Research-supported] [Research: F-GAP-007-02]

#### Acceptance criteria

- **AC-012** (draft) Given an audit record exists, When any user attempts to edit or delete it, Then the original record remains unchanged. [Research: FEA-016 · Research-supported] [Research: F-GAP-007-02]

## 9. State Transitions and Edge Cases

### Supplier lifecycle

State names other than those quoted from the mockup are descriptive labels, not decided names.

| State | Event | Next state | Who can trigger | Provenance |

| Not registered | Supplier submitted for approval | Awaiting approval | Procurement staff | [Customer: FEA-002 · Explicit] [Mockup: SCR-003 · Observed] |

| Awaiting approval | Rejected | Returned to registrant | Unknown (who may reject is not stated) | [Customer: FEA-009 · Explicit] |
| Returned to registrant | Details corrected and resubmitted | Awaiting approval | The registrant | [Customer: FEA-009 · Explicit] |
| Awaiting approval | Phone check finds bank details do not match | Unknown (rejection or a separate on-hold state; supplier cannot be approved until corrected) | Finance approver | [Customer: FEA-008 · Explicit] |
| Awaiting approval | Supplier cannot be reached by phone | Unknown | Unknown | [Inferred: FEA-008 · Unknown] |
| Approved | Bank details changed | Unknown | Unknown | [Inferred: FEA-010 · Unknown] |
| Awaiting approval | Duplicate VAT number submitted | Blocked at registration; no supplier created | Procurement staff | [Customer: FEA-004 · Explicit] |

Edge cases not decided: simultaneous submission of the same supplier, simultaneous approve and reject, notification failure, upload failure (see section 16).

## 10. Non-Functional Requirements

- **NFR-001** How long audit records are kept is set by the organisation's policy rather than by the user interface; the customer's retention policy has not been obtained. Low confidence: generic fixture guidance. [Research: FEA-017 · Research-supported] [Research: F-GAP-007-03]

No performance, availability or compliance requirements are available: no input or kept evidence states any.

- **BR-002** One approval is enough to approve a supplier. [Customer: FEA-001 · Explicit] [Decision: DEC-002]
- **BR-003** A supplier that has not been approved must not be payable. [Customer: FEA-006 · Explicit]
- **BR-004** A supplier whose bank details do not match the phone confirmation cannot be approved until the details are corrected. [Customer: FEA-008 · Explicit] [Decision: DEC-001]

# Stage 15: Review and validate

Goal: the specification checked mechanically and reviewed independently, with at most two
revision rounds. Failed checks stay failed. §9.13, §7 Stage 15.

## Steps

1. `run_state.py verify`, `run_state.py stage 15 --run <run-id> --start`. Round = 1.
2. `<python> <skill_dir>/scripts/check_spec.py --run <run-id> --round <round>` (exit 1 means
   blocking [code] failures; a result, not an error).
3. Agent tool, `subagent_type: doc-reviewer`, prompt:

   ```
   Run ID: <run-id>
   Run directory: <absolute run dir>
   Round: <round>
   Write: <run dir>/review.json (schema: review).
   Warnings, if any: <run dir>/warnings/doc-reviewer.json.
   ```

   `validate.py review <run dir>/review.json`; one retry with errors.
4. If `validation.json` has `blocking_failures` or `review.json` has `passed: false`, and fewer
   than `review.revision_rounds` (config, 2) revisions were made:
   1. Agent tool, `subagent_type: doc-writer`, `Mode: revise`, same run details, fix list:
      "apply every failing item in <run dir>/validation.json and every fix in <run dir>/review.json".
   2. `run_state.py record-revision --run <run-id>` (records the new spec version; refuses if
      the spec changed without a doc-writer invocation).
   3. `status_rules.py register spec.md --run <run-id>` and `status_rules.py labels --run <run-id>`
      (new ASM-W items first).
   4. Round += 1; repeat from step 2.
5. `run_state.py stage 15 --run <run-id> --complete`. It refuses while blocking checks fail and
   revision rounds remain. When both rounds are used and failures remain, it completes: the
   publication status will be `not_fully_validated` and the failures are listed. Never weaken a
   check, edit `validation.json` or `review.json`, or describe a failed review as passed.
6. Unless the post-review Checkpoint 13R already ran in this run: if change-impact analysis
   has made approved items stale after Stage 13 (including a
   `change_after_checkpoint_3` in a `--non-interactive` run)
   (`status_rules.py labels` → `stale_approved`), run Checkpoint 13R now (allowed once after
   review); it marks Stages 14–16 for one re-run, which you then perform (Stages 14 and 15
   again). Items going stale after that stay Stale.

## Report

Per round: [code] failures, reviewer blocking failures and warnings, fixes applied; final
state of both checks.

1	# Supplier Onboarding (New supplier registration and approval): Feature Specification
2	
3	## 1. Document Status
4	
5	- Run ID: 20261012-055017-ac3509
6	- Date: 2026-10-12
7	- Run mode: fixture
8	- Publication status: pending final pass
9	- Known limitations: Capture covers one page only (the New supplier form); no confirmation, error, empty or loading states, and no approver or verification screens, were captured. Research on bank detail changes after approval found no citable source (sources paywalled, members-only or off-topic). Research on audit records found only low-confidence generic fixture guidance, not COSO or UK audit practice; one finding was dropped in verification. Research for the deferred gaps was not performed.
10	- Open stale items: none
11	- Unresolved blocking issues: Q-001, Q-002, Q-003, Q-004 and Q-005 are blocking and unanswered (see section 16).
12	
13	## 2. Executive Summary
14	
15	This feature lets Procurement staff register a new supplier (company name, VAT number and bank details) and requires a Finance team member to approve it before the supplier can be paid. The customer also requires bank details to be verified before approval. The customer's answers say verification is a phone call to the supplier on a number from an independent source, that one approval from any Finance team member is enough, that the approver must differ from the registrant, and that a rejected supplier goes back to its registrant to correct and resubmit.
16	
17	The only mockup screen captured is the registration form. It does not show where Finance verifies and approves, how payment is blocked, what the registrant sees after submitting, or how bank details are entered (the form has a file upload, while the customer defined three fields). Key open decisions are listed in section 16; five of them block a complete specification: where review and approval happen, how unapproved suppliers are kept from payment, what happens when bank details change after approval, what a failed phone check means, and how bank details are entered.
18	
19	## 3. Goals and Scope
20	
21	### Goals
22	
23	- Procurement staff can register new suppliers with company name, VAT number and bank details. [Customer: REQ-001 · Conflicting]
24	- A new supplier cannot be paid until a Finance team member other than the registrant has approved it. [Customer: FEA-001 · Explicit] [Customer: FEA-006 · Explicit]
25	- Bank details are phone-verified before approval. [Customer: FEA-008 · Explicit]
26	
27	### In Scope
28	
29	- Supplier registration by Procurement staff, including the format-only VAT check and duplicate VAT blocking. [Customer: FEA-003 · Explicit] [Customer: FEA-004 · Explicit]
30	- Phone verification of bank details, approval by one Finance team member, and rejection with return to the registrant. [Customer: FEA-008 · Explicit] [Customer: FEA-001 · Explicit] [Customer: FEA-009 · Explicit]
31	- The approved gaps in section 7 (GAP-001 to GAP-007, GAP-009 and GAP-011) are in scope to be resolved; none is resolved yet.
32	
33	### Out of Scope / Rejected
34	
35	Information unavailable: no decision rejected an item and the customer's requirements excluded nothing. Exclusions are not inferred from absence in the mockup.
36	
37	### Deferred
38	
39	- GAP-008 (Deferred: DEC-005): who may register, view and edit suppliers and their bank details, and how long bank details and rejected registrations are kept.
40	- GAP-010 (Deferred: DEC-005): non-UK suppliers, accepted VAT number formats and required fields.
41	- GAP-012 (Deferred: DEC-005): accessibility of form errors, status messages and the file chooser.
42	
43	## 4. Users and Roles
44	
45	- Procurement staff register new suppliers. [Customer: FEA-002 · Explicit]
46	- Finance team members can approve a new supplier; one approval is enough; a finance approver phones the supplier to verify bank details. [Customer: FEA-001 · Explicit] [Customer: FEA-008 · Explicit]
47	- Unknown: whether people outside Procurement staff are prevented from registering, whether a Finance team member who is also Procurement staff may register, and how the product identifies Finance and Procurement members. [Assumption: ASM-G-002 · Assumption]
48	- Unknown: whether the product can identify the individual who registers and the individual who approves. [Assumption: ASM-F-001 · Assumption]
49	
50	## 5. Existing Mockup Coverage
51	
52	- SCR-001 "New supplier" screen: a form with Company name and VAT number text inputs, a Bank details file chooser and a Submit for approval button; observed state is the default empty form only. [Mockup: SCR-001 · Observed]
53	- SCR-002 form component: no field shows a required marker; the action "Submit for approval" is a button that is not visibly disabled. [Mockup: SCR-002 · Observed]
54	- SCR-003 flow: the Submit for approval button has no target, so the destination after submitting is not shown. [Mockup: SCR-003 · Observed]
55	- SCR-004 Supplier data entity: Company name, VAT number and Bank details are visible fields; Approval status is inferred and not visible. [Mockup: SCR-004 · Observed]
56	- Ambiguous behaviours not answered by the mockup: required fields and validation rules; accepted file types, sizes and storage for Bank details; who can view bank details after upload; what happens on submit, on failure, and on resubmission; downstream changes and notifications.
57	- Capture limitation: one page captured with status complete; no confirmation, error, empty or loading states beyond the default form. Other screens may exist that were not captured. [Assumption: ASM-G-001 · Assumption]
58	
59	## 6. Requirements Traceability
60	
61	| REQ | Requirement | Treatment | Label | References |
62	|---|---|---|---|---|
63	| REQ-001 | Procurement staff register new suppliers with company name, VAT number and bank details. | partially addressed | Conflicting | FR-001, FR-004, FR-005, FR-006, FR-007, FR-013, FR-014, FR-017; DEC-004 |
64	| REQ-002 | A finance approver must approve a new supplier before it can be paid. | partially addressed | Unknown | FR-002, FR-008, FR-009, FR-011, FR-012, FR-015; DEC-002, DEC-003 |
65	| REQ-003 | Bank details must be verified before approval. | partially addressed | Unknown | FR-003, FR-010, FR-016; DEC-001 |

67	## 7. Gaps Identified
68	
69	| GAP | Gap | Approval | Path | Priority | Status | Rationale |
70	|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
71	| GAP-001 | Approval and bank-detail verification steps not shown in the capture | Approved: DEC-005 | customer | critical | open (customer decision pending: Q-001) | The capture shows only the registrant's form. |
72	| GAP-002 | How payment is blocked until a supplier is approved | Approved: DEC-005 | customer | critical | open (customer decision pending: Q-002) | No document says where payments are made or how an unapproved supplier is stopped. |
73	| GAP-003 | Bank details changed after approval | Approved: DEC-005 | both | critical | open (researched; customer decision pending: Q-003) | Research found no citable source; DEC-003 did not answer this part. |

77	| GAP-007 | Traceability of registration, verification and approval | Approved: DEC-005 | both | important | open (researched; customer decision pending: Q-006) | Two low-confidence findings kept; framework question unanswered. |

80	| GAP-010 | Non-UK suppliers and field formats | Deferred: DEC-005 | both | important | open (deferred by DEC-005) | Deferred by the customer. |
81	| GAP-011 | Duplicate and simultaneous submissions | Approved: DEC-005 | customer | optional | open (customer decision pending: Q-008) | Which records count as existing is not stated. |
82	| GAP-012 | Accessibility of the registration form errors and file upload | Deferred: DEC-005 | research | optional | open (deferred by DEC-005) | Deferred by the customer. |

84	## 8. Functional Requirements
85	
86	### Supplier registration

88	Procurement staff register a new supplier on the New supplier form and submit it for approval.

[Customer: FEA-003 · Explicit] [Decision: DEC-004]
111	- **AC-002** Given a Procurement staff member on the New supplier form, When they submit a VAT number that fails the format check, Then no supplier is created; the message wording is undecided (FR-014). [Customer: FEA-003 · Explicit] [Decision: DEC-004]
112	- **AC-003** Given an existing supplier with VAT number V, When a Procurement staff member submits a new supplier with VAT number V, Then the submission is blocked and no new supplier is created; whether pending or rejected suppliers count as existing is undecided (FR-017). 115	
116	A Finance team member phones the supplier to verify bank details and then approves or rejects the supplier.

120	- **FR-002** A finance approver must approve a new supplier before it can be paid. [Customer: REQ-002 · Unknown] [Decision: DEC-002]
121	- **FR-003** Bank details must be verified before approval. [Customer: REQ-003 · Unknown] [Decision: DEC-001]
122	- **FR-008** Only members of the Finance team can approve a new supplier; one approval is sufficient; the approver must be a different person from whoever registered the supplier. [Customer: FEA-001 · Explicit] [Decision: DEC-002]
123	- **FR-010** Before approval, a finance approver phones the supplier on a number from an independent source and confirms the bank details; if they do not match, the supplier cannot be approved until the details are corrected. [Customer: FEA-008 · Explicit] [Decision: DEC-001]
124	- **FR-011** A rejected supplier goes back to the person who registered it, who can correct the details and resubmit it. [Customer: FEA-009 · Explicit] [Decision: DEC-003]
